def: The set of data, systems and people affected if one component misbehaves.
The combination of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and the ability to communicate externally, which lets an injection steal data.
A design rule that an agent session should have at most two of: untrusted input, sensitive access, and the ability to change state or communicate externally.
A restriction on what an agent can do, such as narrow tools, scoped credentials, allow-lists or sandboxes, that holds whatever the model decides.
A design in which a privileged model plans and uses tools without seeing untrusted text, and a quarantined model without tools reads it, passing results as variables.
A pattern in which the agent fixes its sequence of tool calls before reading any untrusted data.
A pattern in which the model only chooses among a fixed set of predefined actions and never sees tool output.
A defence that takes control flow only from the trusted request and tracks the provenance of every value, enforcing policies in an interpreter before tool calls.
Metadata recording where a value came from and which other values it was derived from.
A rule written in code that allows, denies or asks a person about a tool call, given its arguments and their provenance.
A list of the only hosts or addresses an agent or its client may send requests to, blocking data leaving through other destinations.
The habit of approving prompts without reading them when they are too frequent or too vague, which turns a human gate into a rubber stamp.
